metadata.title: Figures Only Where the Text Supports Them
metadata.note: Week 3 progress report. Voice hai/Bella for @HumanitariansAI. Counts and findings only from the CAJAL reports for chapters 30, 31 and 13; nothing invented for chapters 23, 6 and 9.
metadata.author: Risa Samanta

beats.narration_text: Before a textbook figure gets drawn, someone has to decide which figures should exist. This is Risa Samanta's progress report for the week: CAJAL scan reports for chapters twenty-three, thirty, thirteen, thirty-one, six and nine.

props.command: claude "/scan chapter 30: propose figures, and reject anything the text cannot support"

beats.narration_text: Every report opens with the same header: sections scanned, figures proposed, and video candidates. Chapter thirty proposes sixty-five figures, fifty-five new and ten already in the text, with two video candidates. Chapter thirty-one proposes fifty, thirty-nine new and eleven existing, and no video candidates.

props.title: report headers: chapters 30 and 31
props.code:
## Chapter 30: Future Directions in Cancer Treatment Research
**Sections scanned:** 30.1 through 30.8 (+ Summary)
**Figures proposed:** 65 (55 new + 10 existing)
**Video candidates:** 2

## Chapter 31: Solid Tumors by Organ/System
**Sections scanned:** 31.1 through 31.9
**Figures proposed:** 50 (39 new + 11 existing)
**Video candidates:** 0
props.sparkLine: A proposal is a number you can check.

beats.narration_text: The rule behind every report is simple. A figure is only proposed when the chapter text gives it something concrete to show, a mechanism, a table, or a dataset. Everything else is rejected, and each rejection carries a written reason.

props.command: claude "propose a figure only if the text gives me a mechanism, a table or a dataset. otherwise reject it and say why"

beats.narration_text: The scan also finds problems in the source. In chapter thirteen, section thirteen point five point four, on peritoneal metastasis, appears twice with identical text. And the chapter names cerebrospinal fluid spread as a metastatic route, then never explains it. The report flags both instead of working around them. It also found one video candidate: the CSF1 macrophage loop in section thirteen point eight point three, which the text itself calls a paracrine feed-forward loop.
beats.visual_intent: Real drifted caption names from the actual repo animating toward a clean sectioned scheme. Show the mechanism, not a count.

beats.narration_text: The method is the same in every chapter. Read every section, propose a figure only where the text supports one, reject the rest with a reason, and write down what is wrong in the source. The same scan covered chapters twenty-three, six and nine.

props.command: claude "summarize what the scan decided, and what it found wrong in the source"

beats.narration_text: Your turn. If you review figures for a long document, give Claude the sections, ask it to propose a figure only where the text supports one, and make it reject the rest with a reason. Then read the rejections as carefully as the proposals.

props.command: claude "here are the sections. propose figures only where the text supports one. reject the rest and say why"

beats.narration_text: Figures only where the text supports them. This has been Risa Samanta's report, voiced by Bella for Humanitarians AI. Read the rejections as closely as the proposals.
